audit_findings.title: Capitalized interest may escape the current owner-earnings charge
audit_findings.mechanism: Potential omission from FY2025 owner earnings and therefore from the $127.9 million anchor and all forecast periods
audit_findings.evidence: As our qualifying assets exceeded our outstanding debt during the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, we capitalized all interest costs incurred on these facilities during these periods.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved mapping possibility, not a demonstrated omission. FY2025 filings show $81.3 million of cash interest paid, $77.323 million capitalized, $60.738 million released through cost of sales, and a $16.585 million increase in capitalized interest inventory. Those amounts are large relative to the $127.9 million anchor, so an unreconciled portion could materially reduce value. A cash-flow-based OE calculation may already capture capitalization through inventory changes, but the supplied record does not demonstrate that reconciliation.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile cash interest paid by facility to interest expensed, interest capitalized, interest released through cost of sales, Century Living development assets, and every inventory or working-capital adjustment in FY2025 OE; rerun all scenarios for any net omitted cash interest.

audit_findings.title: The cash bridge may add operating liquidity as though it were excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $92.334 million, equal to $3.07 per share and 4.9% of the $1.889 billion base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Excess-asset bridge adds cash separately after operating value
audit_findings.evidence: We use funds generated by operations, available borrowings under our revolving line of credit, and proceeds from issuances of debt or equity to fund our short-term working capital obligations and fund our purchases of land, as well as land development, home construction activities, and other cash needs.
audit_findings.explanation: The valuation demonstrably adds all $92.334 million of June 2026 cash, but the filings demonstrate that cash supports seasonal land, construction, mortgage-origination, and other working-capital needs. The record does not establish how much is excess. The maximum exposure is large enough to affect per-share value and the margin-of-safety threshold, so the classification issue is materially open.
audit_findings.action: Establish minimum unrestricted operating cash using monthly seasonal cash balances, construction commitments, Financial Services funding needs, covenant liquidity, and revolver usage; add only the residual excess cash and rerun the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Century Living's changed asset-disposition model may not fit the standard OE mapping
audit_findings.mechanism: May distort normalized OE and growth if sale earnings are forecast without matching replacement-development investment
audit_findings.evidence: During the first quarter of 2025, our strategy evolved for our Century Living multi-family rental properties to be predominantly focused on the disposition of the assets shortly after lease stabilization.
audit_findings.explanation: The business-model change and FY2025 property sale are demonstrated, but a valuation error is not. Century Living produced $97.2 million of sales revenue, $5.351 million of gross sale profit, and $4.869 million of FY2025 pretax segment income, only 3.8% of the $127.9 million anchor at the pretax-income scale. However, Century Living inventory increased from $188.543 million at year-end 2025 to $232.297 million at June 2026, showing continuing capital deployment. The record does not establish whether OE captured that investment or whether forecasts assume replacement versus runoff, so the sustainable value effect remains unquantified.
audit_findings.action: Trace the sold property's revenue, cost, capitalized interest, debt repayment, development expenditures, inventory movements, and proceeds through FY2025 OE; then separately rerun replacement and runoff treatments for Century Living.

audit_findings.title: The FY2025 anchor contains an expiring tax benefit
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.737 million FY2025 benefit; computed approximately $38.4 million of base equity value, $1.28 per share, and $0.90 of buy-below value
audit_findings.mechanism: An expiring tax credit is embedded in anchor OE and propagated through forecast and terminal earnings
audit_findings.evidence: The “One Big Beautiful Bill,” enacted July 4, 2025, eliminates these credits for homes delivered after June 30, 2026, and recent certification changes may make claiming the credit before expiration more difficult or uneconomical.
audit_findings.explanation: The benefit and its expiration after June 30, 2026 are demonstrated. Removing $2.737 million equals 2.1% of the $127.9 million anchor and, under the supplied linear DCF, reduces base value from about $62.91 to $61.63 per share and buy-below from $44.04 to about $43.14. It does not reverse the bear, base, or bull relationship to the $64.51 market price and is therefore not material to the stated valuation conclusion, although it should be corrected.
audit_findings.action: Remove the Section 45L benefit from normalized OE after June 2026 and confirm the forecast tax rate; rerun the scenarios to record the approximately $1.28 base per-share reduction.

audit_findings.title: Long-tail construction claims could exceed the expense already recognized
audit_findings.mechanism: Future adverse reserve development would reduce OE or create an additional claim on equity
audit_findings.evidence: Though state regulations vary, construction defect claims are reported and resolved over a long period of time, which can extend for 10 years or more.
audit_findings.explanation: No reserve deficiency is demonstrated. CCS had a filed $45.584 million self-insurance reserve at June 30, 2026, up from $42.119 million at year-end, recorded $4.980 million of first-half provisions, and reported no first-half actuarial adjustment. Existing estimated claims are therefore already represented in the accounts; only future adverse development beyond those estimates would affect value.
audit_findings.action: Monitor actuarial reserve studies, paid and incurred claim triangles by delivery vintage, insurance recoveries, retentions, exclusions, policy limits, and subsequent reserve adjustments; rerun OE only if adverse development becomes filed or reliably estimable.
